claim: Prompt engineering is described in one survey as a technique that strategically designs task-specific instructions, referred to as prompts, to guide model output without altering parameters.
quote: Prompt engineering has emerged as a crucial technique for enhancing the capabilities of pre-trained large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). It involves strategically designing task-specific instructions, referred to as prompts, to guide model output without altering parameters.

claim: One paper describes prompts as instructions given to an LLM to enforce rules, automate processes, and ensure specific qualities (and quantities) of generated output.
quote: Prompts are instructions given to an LLM to enforce rules, automate processes, and ensure specific qualities (and quantities) of generated output.

claim: The same paper adds that prompts are also a form of programming that can customize the outputs and interactions with an LLM.
quote: Prompts are also a form of programming that can customize the outputs and interactions with an LLM.

claim: Context management has also become a concrete concern for agents: one study notes that LLM agents on long-running tasks inevitably exceed their usable context window, forcing a choice about what history to discard.
quote: Large language model (LLM) agents operating on long-running tasks inevitably exceed their usable context window, forcing a choice about what history to discard.

claim: The agentic variant is said to embed autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline.
quote: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG) transcends these limitations by embedding autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline.

claim: One survey reports that changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.
quote: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings

claim: Another paper defines scaling the harness as treating the structured execution layer around a foundation model as a first-class object of design, evaluation, and optimization.
quote: We refer to this shift as scaling the harness: treating the structured execution layer around a foundation model as a first-class object of design, evaluation, and optimization.

claim: A separate survey states that it takes the agent loop, not the model in isolation, as its unit of analysis.
quote: Every LLM agent, beneath its framework and its prompts, runs a loop: it observes, decides, acts, and observes again until it stops. This survey takes that agent loop, not the model in isolation, as its unit of analysis, on the argument that the properties practitioners actually care about, cost, reliability, and safety, are decided by the loop rather than by the model alone.

claim: One survey states that prompt engineering involves strategically designing task-specific instructions, referred to as prompts, to guide model output without altering parameters.
quote: Prompt engineering has emerged as a crucial technique for enhancing the capabilities of pre-trained large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). It involves strategically designing task-specific instructions, referred to as prompts, to guide model output without altering parameters.

claim: A separate wireless-networks overview defines the perspective as designing prompts to guide LLMs to generate desired output without updating LLM parameters.
quote: These adaptations can be extremely demanding for computational resources and datasets, while most network devices have limited computation power, and there are a limited number of high-quality networking datasets. To this end, this work explores LLM-enabled wireless networks from the prompt engineering perspective, that is, designing prompts to guide LLMs to generate desired output without updating LLM parameters.

claim: The prompt pattern catalog frames prompts as a form of programming that can customize the outputs and interactions with an LLM.
quote: Prompts are also a form of programming that can customize the outputs and interactions with an LLM.

claim: The Prompt Report describes the field as suffering from conflicting terminology and a fragmented ontological understanding of what constitutes an effective prompt.
quote: Although prompt engineering is a widely adopted and extensively researched area, it suffers from conflicting terminology and a fragmented ontological understanding of what constitutes an effective prompt due to its relatively recent emergence.

claim: The Prompt Report, a systematic survey of prompt engineering techniques, presents a vocabulary of 33 terms and a taxonomy of 58 LLM prompting techniques.
quote: We present a detailed vocabulary of 33 vocabulary terms, a taxonomy of 58 LLM prompting techniques, and 40 techniques for other modalities.

claim: A practitioner-focused study calls prompt engineering a critical yet loosely defined skill.
quote: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly embedded in professional and everyday workflows, prompt engineering has emerged as a critical yet loosely defined skill.

claim: The Prompt Report's authors adopt an observational stance and make no claims to the validity of the presented techniques.
quote: Last, our stance is primarily observational, and we make no claims to the validity of the presented techniques.

claim: The ACE authors describe context adaptation as modifying inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence rather than weight updates.
quote: Large language model (LLM) applications such as agents and domain-specific reasoning increasingly rely on context adaptation: modifying inputs with instructions, strategies, or evidence, rather than weight updates.

claim: The ACE framework treats contexts as evolving playbooks that accumulate, refine, and organize strategies through generation, reflection, and curation.
quote: We introduce ACE (Agentic Context Engineering), a framework that treats contexts as evolving playbooks that accumulate, refine, and organize strategies through a modular process of generation, reflection, and curation.

claim: The survey in R2 frames the field as a shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration, and it names context dilution and computational overhead as persistent limitations.
quote: By analyzing the shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration, we identify persistent limitations, such as context dilution and computational overhead.

claim: The Code as Agent Harness paper draws the boundary by saying that prompt engineering changes instructions while context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model.
quote: Whereas prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model, AHE treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis, including tool schemas, planning artifacts, memory policies, retrieval strategies, sandbox configuration, verification sensors, permission tiers, routing rules, multiagent workflows, and human-review gates [281,178].
locator: sec. Agentic Harness Engineering for Adaptive Harness Optimization, para 96

claim: The externalization review calls the harness's separation of the prompt into layers a structured form of context engineering.
quote: From a broader perspective, this tripartite organization of the model boundary-contextual input, instructional input, and action schema-can be understood as a structured form of context engineering.
locator: sec. The LLM Input/Output Perspective, para 241

claim: The harness-scaling paper lists a context constructor as one of six components of an agent.
quote: Under this view, an agent is not simply a model with a prompt, but a system composed of six interacting components: a reasoning substrate (R), a memory store (M), a context constructor (C), a skill-routing layer (S, which dispatches tools and subagents), an orchestration loop (O), and a verification and governance layer (G).

claim: R20 describes context rot as the progressive and nonlinear degradation of agent reasoning quality and tool calling reliability as the context window fills during extended coding sessions.
quote: the progressive and nonlinear degradation of agent reasoning quality and tool calling reliability as the context window fills during extended coding sessions

claim: In a forced-compression experiment, summarize-oldest reached 94.2% recall, keep-most-relevant 60.0%, and drop-oldest 41.7%.
quote: Across 20 independent trials (360 graded queries), summarize-oldest achieves 94.2% overall recall accuracy, keep-most-relevant achieves 60.0%, and drop-oldest achieves only 41.7% (χ 2 = 75.17, p &lt; 0.00001).

claim: The R18 authors acknowledge that their setup is synthetic, single-model, and single-budget.
quote: We discuss the practical implications for agent framework design and the limitations of our synthetic, single-model, single-budget setup.

claim: The survey on harness engineering for LLM agents understands the agent harness as the external execution support structure built around the model.
quote: We understand the agent harness as the external execution support structure built around the model and treat it as a distinct performance lever that complements base model capability

claim: The scaling-the-harness paper says an agent is not simply a model with a prompt, but a system of six interacting components, including a memory store, a context constructor, a skill-routing layer, an orchestration loop, and a verification and governance layer.
quote: Under this view, an agent is not simply a model with a prompt, but a system composed of six interacting components: a reasoning substrate (R), a memory store (M), a context constructor (C), a skill-routing layer (S, which dispatches tools and subagents), an orchestration loop (O), and a verification and governance layer (G).

claim: The externalization review assigns the roles differently: memory externalizes state across time, skills externalize procedural expertise, protocols externalize interaction structure, and harness engineering unifies them into governed execution.
quote: Under this view, memory externalizes state across time, skills externalize procedural expertise, protocols externalize interaction structure, and harness engineering serves as the unification layer that coordinates them into governed execution.

claim: The Agentic Harness Engineering section states that prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented, whereas harness engineering treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis.
quote: Whereas prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model, AHE treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis
locator: sec. Agentic Harness Engineering for Adaptive Harness Optimization, para 96

claim: The externalization review describes the harness's layered model boundary as a structured form of context engineering.
quote: From a broader perspective, this tripartite organization of the model boundary-contextual input, instructional input, and action schema-can be understood as a structured form of context engineering.
locator: sec. The LLM Input/Output Perspective, para 241

claim: The harness-aware evaluation survey reports that changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.
quote: recent results highlight the importance of the agent harness: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.

claim: The scaling-the-harness paper cites SWE-agent as showing that careful tool-schema design alone can improve benchmark accuracy substantially even with a fixed backbone model.
quote: research-side harnesses such as SWE-agent further show that careful tool-schema design alone can improve benchmark accuracy substantially even with a fixed backbone model [40].

claim: The harness-engineering survey also describes a shifting boundary in which routine capability-bearing support migrates into model weights while constraint-bearing governance functions remain external.
quote: explaining the shifting functional boundary where routine capability-bearing support migrates inward into model weights while constraint-bearing governance functions remain external.

claim: The agent-loop survey states that every LLM agent, beneath its framework and its prompts, runs a loop in which it observes, decides, acts, and observes again until it stops.
quote: Every LLM agent, beneath its framework and its prompts, runs a loop: it observes, decides, acts, and observes again until it stops.

claim: The Code as Agent Harness survey says that, rather than exposing the model to a flat list of tools, recent systems wrap it in a managed development loop that controls repository access, file edits, command execution, approval boundaries, context isolation, logging, and validation.
quote: Rather than exposing the model to a flat list of tools, recent systems wrap it in a managed development loop that controls repository access, file edits, command execution, approval boundaries, context isolation, logging, and validation.

claim: The scaling-the-harness paper holds that agent performance emerges from the interaction among the foundation model, memory substrate, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification-and-governance layer.
quote: agent performance emerges from the interaction among the foundation model, memory substrate, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification-and-governance layer.

claim: The externalization review states that in mature agent systems, reliability increasingly depends on external memory stores, tool registries, protocol definitions, sandboxes, sub-agent orchestration, compression pipelines, evaluators, test harnesses, and approval loops.
quote: In mature agent systems, reliability increasingly depends on external memory stores, tool registries, protocol definitions, sandboxes, sub-agent orchestration, compression pipelines, evaluators, test harnesses, and approval loops

claim: The Agentic RAG survey says Agentic RAG transcends the limitations of traditional RAG by embedding autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline.
quote: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG) transcends these limitations by embedding autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline.

claim: The same survey concludes that no single architecture is universally best.
quote: The analysis demonstrates that no single architecture is universally optimal; effectiveness depends on aligning complexity with task requirements.

claim: The RAG-stack review reports that agentic RAG combines agents with RAG pipelines for decision-making, self-optimization and multi-agent coordination.
quote: Agentic and AutoRAG architectures are at the forefront of autonomous AI systems, combining AI agents with RAG pipelines to facilitate dynamic decision-making, self-optimization, and multi-agent coordination [73], [74].
locator: sec. Agentic and AutoRAG Architectures: Autonomous Optimization Systems, para 121

claim: For multi-agent orchestration, the TDD governance paper has the orchestration engine retain authority over state while models only propose.
quote: Large language models act as proposal generators, while an execution engine maintains authority over state mutation and workflow progression.
locator: sec. Proposed Approach and System Description, para 23

claim: The MemTool paper offers autonomous, workflow and hybrid modes, showing that the degree of agent autonomy is a design variable.
quote: MemTool offers three agentic architectures: 1) Autonomous Agent Mode, granting full tool management autonomy, 2) Workflow Mode, providing deterministic control without autonomy, and 3) Hybrid Mode, combining autonomous and deterministic control.

claim: The Agentic RAG survey lists multi-agent coordination, process-aware evaluation and governance among the open challenges.
quote: Substantial open challenges remain in multi-agent coordination, process-aware evaluation, memory management, computational efficiency, and governance.

claim: The Code as Agent Harness survey says that prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model, whereas Agentic Harness Engineering treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis.
quote: Whereas prompt engineering changes instructions and context engineering changes what evidence is presented to the model, AHE treats the operating environment itself as the object of analysis, including tool schemas, planning artifacts, memory policies, retrieval strategies, sandbox configuration, verification sensors, permission tiers, routing rules, multiagent workflows, and human-review gates [281,178].

quote: agent performance emerges from the interaction among the foundation model, memory substrate, context constructor, skill-routing layer, orchestration loop, and verification-and-governance layer.

claim: On evaluation, UniACE argues that a reported score reflects a complete model–harness–environment configuration rather than the model alone.
quote: Agent benchmarks are increasingly used to compare large language models (LLMs) across domains, yet a reported score reflects a complete model--harness--environment configuration rather than the model alone.

claim: The harness-aware evaluation survey reports that changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.
quote: As research pursues more general intelligence, recent results highlight the importance of the agent harness: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.

claim: UniACE's comparisons with source implementations likewise found model-ranking reversals.
quote: Across seven benchmarks, 24 domains, 15 models, 400K rollouts, and 5B tokens, comparisons with source implementations reveal bidirectional score shifts and model-ranking reversals, while matched onlineoffline runs expose sensitivity to accessible evidence and its representation.

claim: The scaling-the-harness paper proposes that future agent benchmarks should additionally measure repeated-use properties such as memory retrieval precision and memory hygiene, and minimal-context efficiency.
quote: The next generation of agent benchmarks should additionally measure repeated-use properties such as memory retrieval precision and memory hygiene, minimalcontext efficiency
locator: sec. From Single Episodes to Longitudinal Evaluation, para 45

claim: The Code as Agent Harness survey cautions that a new retrieval policy may improve benchmark accuracy while increasing hallucinated evidence.
quote: A new retrieval policy may improve benchmark accuracy while increasing hallucinated evidence; a new tool schema may reduce token cost while weakening permission boundaries; a new verifier may improve pass rate by accepting underspecified solutions.
locator: sec. Self-Evolving Harnesses without Regression, para 216

quote: By analyzing the shift from input-level linguistic control to system-level contextual orchestration, we identify persistent limitations, such as context dilution and computational overhead.

claim: The externalization review also says that a common account of why memory, skills and protocols converge, and of how that reshapes the definition of an agent, remains underdeveloped.
quote: What remains underdeveloped is a common account of why these developments are converging as forms of externalization and how that convergence reshapes the definition of an agent.

claim: On evidence, the harness-aware evaluation survey reports that changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.
quote: recent results highlight the importance of the agent harness: changing the execution system around a fixed model can alter performance and even reverse model rankings.

claim: The same survey says that inconsistent reporting of harness configurations, resource budgets, and scoring procedures makes benchmark results difficult to interpret and compare.
quote: Yet inconsistent reporting of harness configurations, resource budgets, and scoring procedures makes benchmark results difficult to interpret and compare.

claim: The context rot study states that no published empirical study has directly tested the joint hypothesis linking codebase scale, context growth and MCP tool attrition.
quote: Despite these convergent findings, no published empirical study has directly tested the joint hypothesis that codebase scale drives context window growth, which in turn triggers measurable MCP tool attrition, defined here as the progressive decline in tool call accuracy, increased first error position, and elevated bug introduction rate during automated debugging.

claim: The Skills Architecture paper reports consistent results across three model families, while stating that it does not claim to have isolated architecture as the sole cause.
quote: Results are consistent across three model families, supporting the position that context rot is architectural in character to a degree that survives cross-model comparison, though we do not claim to have isolated architecture as the sole cause.

claim: The TDD governance paper likewise calls its empirical validation preliminary and says broader cross-model and repository-scale evaluations are needed.
quote: Empirical validation remains preliminary, and broader cross-model and repository-scale evaluations are needed to assess the robustness.
locator: sec. Discussion and Future Work, para 43
